name: Gulf Bank
ownership_summary: Listed on Boursa Kuwait. At 31 Dec 2025 the Group of Warba Bank (through Warba Strategy Co.) held 32.75%, the Public Institution for Social Security 7.19% and Behbehani Investment Co. 6.06% (AR 2025). Warba completed its purchase of Al Ghanem Trading in April 2025, and the two banks signed an MoU in 2025 to assess a merger into one Sharia-compliant bank. The assessment is ongoing: due diligence 'nearing completion' (24 May 2026) and moving 'in an orderly manner' (3 Aug 2026); no definitive agreement found as of 12 Oct 2026. Gulf Bank is separately converting to a Sharia-compliant bank (CBK initial approval Aug 2025).

government_link: Partial - the Public Institution for Social Security (a Kuwaiti public institution) holds 7.19% at 31 Dec 2025; no controlling government holding.
group_structure: Gulf Bank K.S.C.P. consolidates one subsidiary, Gulf Capital Investment Company K.S.C. (Closed), trading as InvestGB (100%, KD 10m capital, established 2023). InvestGB is not profiled separately, so its AUM, people and capabilities are recorded here. Warba Bank (kw-warba) holds 32.75% but does not consolidate Gulf Bank as a subsidiary on the evidence found; do not add the two banks' figures.

footprint: Kuwait: 48 branches and 255+ ATMs per website (30 Jun 2026 context); AR 2025 says 45+ branches, 268 ATMs and 16 ITMs. International Banking department lends across GCC, Turkey and Egypt without local branches (AR 2025).
customer_segments: Mass retail and youth (red, neo), Preferred, Priority (affluent), Private Banking (HNW), SME (11 dedicated SME relationship managers across 11 branches), corporate, multinational, financial institutions and sovereigns. Consumer 34% / corporate and banks 66% of total loans (31 Dec 2025).
business_lines: Consumer Banking (loans, cards, deposits, Preferred, Priority, Private Banking and wealth management), Corporate Banking (wholesale, commercial, SME, structured and project finance, transaction banking), International Banking (financial institutions and sovereigns; multinationals and oil & gas), Treasury and Investment, and InvestGB (asset management, custody, brokerage, wealth, investment banking).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Gulf Bank runs a tiered wealth franchise on top of conventional retail banking: Priority Banking (KD 100,000 to under KD 500,000 of cash or investable assets, or monthly salary of KD 3,500+) with dedicated relationship managers and an investment manager, and invitation-based Private Banking with a dedicated branch and Mastercard World Elite card. Investment services were moved in Nov 2023 into Gulf Capital Investment Company (InvestGB, 100%, CMA-licensed, KD 10m capital), which reports 'managing assets exceeding KD 1 billion'. InvestGB launched its first Sharia-compliant funds (Lulwa KD and USD money market funds) in 2025, runs an Avaloq wealth platform, and has added private-markets partners: Ares Wealth Management Solutions, Arrow Global, Investcorp and, from Jan 2026, CVC (evergreen CVC-PE fund). The bank also offers the WISE advisory/portfolio service (min USD 10,000) and the One Trader app for Boursa Kuwait and regional/global trading. Gulf Bank is converting to a fully Sharia-compliant bank (CBK preliminary approval Aug 2025, final approvals still pending in Aug 2026) and is studying a merger with Warba Bank, which owns 32.75%.

Awarded 'Excellence in Banking Services for High Net Worth Clients in the Middle East' at the Private Banker Awards 2026 (press release 8 Oct 2026). No private-banking asset figure disclosed.

CMA-licensed as portfolio manager, investment advisor, custodian, investment controller, collective investment scheme manager, subscription agent and securities broker not registered on the exchange. Services: asset management, custody and investments, brokerage, wealth management, investment banking. Funds: Lulwa KD and USD Money Market Funds (2025).

brokerage.detail: Online trading via the One Trader app / Boursa Kuwait online trading login: onboarding via mobile, no minimum balance, orders across Boursa Kuwait and 'multiple MENA and global markets', stocks, bonds and ETFs; Boursa Kuwait commission 10 bps (Premier), 15 bps (Main), 30 bps (Auction), minimum 250 fils. The operating entity (bank vs InvestGB) and platform vendor are not stated.

digital_investing.detail: One Trader app (investing onboarding in-app, trade stocks/bonds/ETFs, view portfolio); WISE digital investment platform (goal and risk questionnaire, recommended diversified international portfolios, Sharia-compliant option, USD 10,000 minimum); Lulwa money market funds listed on the personal investment page. The investment hub page still refers to 'Gulf Bank Mobile Trader' (older wording).

advisory.detail: InvestGB is CMA-licensed as investment advisor; Priority clients get 'investment solutions ... guided by our registered Investment Manager'; WISE is described as an advisory and portfolio management service.

discretionary.detail: InvestGB is licensed as portfolio manager (S19) and WISE portfolios are 'monitored and reviewed' by bank investment managers (S21), but no source opened states that WISE or Private Banking portfolios are discretionary.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: WISE: questionnaire on goals, risk tolerance and horizon leads to a recommended diversified international portfolio (conservative, high-risk, income and Islamic variants cited for 2023 returns), built on a 'Nobel Prize-winning investment strategy'; bank-reported 2023 returns 10.7% conservative, 20.9% high-risk, 22% Islamic. Current availability: not listed in the 12 Oct 2026 Investment menu (Online Trading, Lulwa KD, Lulwa USD) although 'WISE Portfolio' remains an accepted loan collateral type.

A public third-party mutual-fund shelf was not found.

Chairman Bader AlKharafi resigned; Ahmad Al Bahar named Chairman by acclamation (new 11-member board elected March 2025). Merger project with Boubyan Bank called off in Jan 2025.

Warba Bank completed its purchase of Al Ghanem Trading, giving it (via Warba Strategy Co.) 32.75% of Gulf Bank; AR 2025 timeline records Warba's letter proposing a merger feasibility study, CBK guidance, and an MoU with Warba Bank for a potential merger during 2025.
CBK granted initial approval, valid for one year, for conversion into a Sharia-compliant bank; Lamia Karam appointed Chairperson of InvestGB.

InvestGB launched its first Sharia-compliant funds (Lulwa KD and USD Money Market Funds); upgraded to an Avaloq wealth platform; partnerships with Ares (WMS), Arrow Global (Q4) and Investcorp. Core banking transformation completed.
InvestGB announced strategic partnership with CVC for private equity access (date per Gulfbase item dated 11 Jan 2026; search result only).
Chief Risk Officer Abdulrahman Al-Saddah's resignation took effect; GM Consumer Banking Bader Al-Ali's resignation took effect 15 Feb 2026 (AR labels it 'Chief Risk Officer', apparently a typo).
Ammar Hajeyah became Chief Investment Officer of InvestGB.

Acting Deputy CEO said Warba merger due diligence is 'nearing completion' and that conversion requirements are being fulfilled before an end-August 2026 regulatory deadline; two Sharia-consent clauses added to customer contracts.
InvestGB expanded its CVC private equity offering (CVC-PE Fund).
Faisal AlAdsani appointed Deputy CEO and Faisal AlGharabally General Manager Corporate and International Banking (effective date).
H1 2026 webcast: Acting CEO describes 'measured progress' on Islamic conversion (still preliminary approval, no deadline given) and the Warba merger moving 'in an orderly manner'.
Annual General Meeting held (AGM documents listed on the IR page; dividend of 9 fils and 5% bonus shares proposed in AR 2025).
Gulf Bank publicised Priority Banking and an award for HNW banking services at the Private Banker Awards 2026. The press-release list shows no merger or conversion announcement up to this date.

opportunities: Strategy 2030 pillars include 'Boost Growth Within Banking' (expanding mortgage, SME and wealth propositions) and 'Expand Beyond Banking' (partnerships and ventures in fintech, embedded finance) (S4 p.12).

Islamic conversion requires a Sharia-compliant product shelf across product, treasury and investment frameworks (S4 p.12-13); InvestGB's first Sharia-compliant funds were only launched in 2025 (S4 p.52).

Digital managed-portfolio offer is limited to WISE (USD 10,000 minimum, bank-reported, 2024) which is no longer listed in the Oct 2026 Investment menu (S11, S21); Priority clients (KD 100,000 to under KD 500,000) are served by relationship managers with 'exclusive investment solutions' (S10, S13).
InvestGB is building a private-markets shelf by adding partners (Ares, Arrow, Investcorp, CVC) and states wealth and asset management expansion as a commitment (S4 p.51, S26).
barriers: Corporate actions in flight: conversion to a Sharia-compliant bank (final approvals pending) and a possible merger with Warba Bank (due diligence 'nearing completion' in May 2026); vendor decisions may wait or be merged with Warba (S8, S15).
InvestGB already runs an Avaloq wealth platform and has an established set of private-markets product partners (S4 p.52, S4 p.51).
Acting leadership: Acting CEO, Acting CRO, Acting GM Consumer Banking; Consumer GM and CRO resigned in early 2026 (S1, S4).
IT capacity: core banking transformation completed in 2025 and the IT workstream is upgrading the core platform for Islamic compliance (S4 p.13).

discrepancies.detail: Press release states customer deposits of KD 6.0 billion; the statement of financial position shows 'Customer deposits' KD 5,073,142k plus 'Deposits from financial institutions' KD 924,721k (total about KD 5,998m).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded KD 5,073,142k (statement label 'Customer deposits'); the press-release figure includes deposits from financial institutions.

discrepancies.field: Status of CBK approval for Islamic conversion
discrepancies.detail: Press-release headline of 24 May 2026 says the bank is preparing 'following the final approval of the Central Bank', but the body says conversion is 'once we obtain final approval' and the H1 2026 webcast (3 Aug 2026) still refers to 'preliminary approval'.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as preliminary approval only (initial approval Aug 2025, valid one year); no final approval found as of 12 Oct 2026.

discrepancies.detail: Website group profile: 48 branches, 255+ ATMs; AR 2025 p.8: 45+ branches, 268 ATMs, 16 ITMs.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded; website used for the branches metric as more recent.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 footnote on p.70 says Bader Al-Ali resigned from 'Chief Risk Officer' effective 15 Feb 2026, but his listed role is General Manager - Consumer Banking (the CRO was Abdulrahman Al-Saddah).
discrepancies.resolution: Read as a typographical error for General Manager - Consumer Banking; consistent with Tarek Ragab now listed as Acting GM Consumer Banking (S1).

discrepancies.detail: 24 May 2026 release calls Faisal AlAdsani 'Acting Deputy CEO'; the website lists 'Deputy CEO' and Kuwait Times reports the appointment effective 9 Jul 2026.
'Assets exceeding KD 1 billion' appears both at the Nov 2023 launch and in AR 2025; the wording is 'manages assets' not 'AUM' and is a floor, not a dated balance.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as aum with status Requires verification.

discrepancies.field: Faisal AlAdsani - acting deputy start and earlier grade
discrepancies.detail: Gulf Bank's 9 Jul 2026 release says Acting Deputy CEO 'since 2023' and General Manager, Corporate Banking Group 2021-2023; its 28 Aug 2023 release says Deputy GM Corporate Banking 2021-2023, then promoted to GM Corporate Banking. Mahfouz was styled Acting Deputy CEO on 14 Oct 2023 and Deputy CEO on 31 Jul 2024.
discrepancies.resolution: 2023 release used for the Deputy GM and GM steps; 'acting since 2023' kept as the bank's wording; actual start of the acting deputy role unreconciled.

discrepancies.field: Date Sami Mahfouz became Acting CEO
discrepancies.detail: Mandani is quoted as Acting CEO on 27 Jul 2025; Mahfouz presented as Acting CEO on 29 Oct 2025; no announcement found.
discrepancies.resolution: Appointed recorded as 2025 with the bracket in appointed_note.

discrepancies.field: Chairman Al Bahar and Dalal AlRayes - wording differences
discrepancies.detail: Al Bahar: Board page says former Chairman of 'Bahrain Real Estate Company' and a degree in Business Administration and Finance; AR 2025 p.60 says 'First Bahrain Co.' and BSc Business Administration. AlRayes: Board page 'Business Administration (Finance and Economics)'; AR p.64 'Business Management' (Babson College).
discrepancies.resolution: AR wording used for degrees (higher tier); both company names kept.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 p.72 lists a Chief Information Officer and p.89 shows an unnamed Acting Chief Digital Transformation Officer; the Executive Management page read on 2026-10-13 lists neither, and a search snippet of the executives page showed a different Acting CIO name that is not on the page as read.
discrepancies.resolution: Unresolved; no IT or digital head added. Najla Aleisa (CMO, leads digital strategy) added instead.
